body:
Simulate 30 agents with realistic submission intervals, gate duration, failure, flake, conflict and priority mix before choosing queue and recovery defaults.

- [ ] Compare sequential, pipeline-K and batch-M using seeded reproducible scenarios. Pipeline-2 must beat sequential at agreed realistic failure rates or the design changes.
- [ ] Compare 5,15,30-minute fix-forward windows with immediate revert on time-to-green and changes stacked on red; include fix gate attempts and mandatory full confirmation within the bounded incident.
- [ ] Publish p50/p95 time-to-land per class, utilization, speculative waste, preemption count, inheritance/aging behavior and human grant cost. Recommend mode,slots and fix_window; maintainer acceptance remains required.
- [ ] Prove no class starves under stated admissible-load assumptions, including sustained arrivals, repeated sev work and dependency chains. An overloaded system cannot promise bounded waiting; report overload explicitly.
- [ ] Model audited grants/expiry, max_sev_in_flight including inherited dependencies, grace-period lease transfer and attempt-only slot preemption; no cap deadlock or fabricated pass.
- [ ] Preserve exact pipeline evidence and weaker batch scope; retries stay on same candidate. Confirm culprits before compensation and never auto-revert from flaky/inconclusive attribution.
- [ ] Commit throwaway simulator/report under docs/spikes/; no product code or qualification success is claimed.
title: S4: qualify priority scheduling and bounded fix-forward economics
